rows.evidence: Q1: Study Area and Results sections - the authors apply their own RASGEMINEC model (simulated annealing + EPANET + Monte Carlo) to a 191 ha citrus network in Valencia with 385 hydrants and report their own model runs (Tables 1-4) for energy consumption under three operating modes.
rows.notes: The study does not report any result on water use, over- or under-irrigation of plots, or water management efficiency. It assumes a single irrigation time (tr = 3.29 h) and a single application rate for all hydrants, and optimises only pumping energy. What it actually shows is that SA-optimised sectoring reduced modelled daily energy consumption by 11.7% versus on-demand operation and 15.5% versus elevation-based sectoring, and reduced instantaneous power by 38.3% and 21.6%. The claimed water-inefficiency consequence of uniform irrigation times is the review's own inference about the design of such sectoring schedules, not a finding of this paper. Model outputs were not compared with measured energy or water data.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The paper is a modelling study of energy-minimising sectoring of a pressurised drip network; it contains no measurement or assessment of water conservation or plot-level water adequacy.
